questions.question: You are part of a research team. Your supervisor asks you to slightly modify some results so that they align better with the organisation’s expectations. You know the original results are accurate but may affect future approvals. What should you do?
questions.questionHtml: You are part of a research team. Your supervisor asks you to slightly modify some results so that they align better with the organisation’s expectations. You know the original results are accurate but may affect future approvals. What should you do?

options.text: Modify the results as instructed to maintain good relations and ensure approvals.
options.html: Modify the results as instructed to maintain good relations and ensure approvals.

options.text: Refuse to alter the accurate results, present the findings honestly, and document your concern appropriately.
options.html: Refuse to alter the accurate results, present the findings honestly, and document your concern appropriately.

options.text: Change the results but privately inform a colleague about the real findings.
options.html: Change the results but privately inform a colleague about the real findings.

options.text: Submit only partial data so that the full picture is unclear.
options.html: Submit only partial data so that the full picture is unclear.

questions.solution:
Explanation:

The correct approach is to maintain integrity and professional ethics.

Altering accurate research results to match expectations is unethical and can damage credibility, trust, and long-term professional reputation. Research must be presented honestly, even if the findings are inconvenient.

Refusing to modify valid data, presenting the results accurately, and documenting your concern ensures transparency and protects both personal and organisational integrity.

options.html: The film has been completed by the famous director by next month.

questions.solution:
Answer: (c) The film will have been completed by the famous director by next month.

Explanation:
The given sentence is in Future Perfect Tense.

Structure:
Active → Subject + will have + V3 + object
Passive → Object + will have been + V3 + by + subject

Active sentence:
The famous director will have completed the film by next month.

Passive sentence:
The film will have been completed by the famous director by next month.

Therefore, the correct option is (c).

questions.question: Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. S1: There was a woman on the station platform. A tall scrag of a woman wearing a little round hat with a brown feather that dropped in a draggled fringe over her eyes. A. The toss and tumble, the hurrying threading rush of movement left her high and dry. B. Brown button boots showed under the skirt and an end of white petticoat dabbled with mud. C. Round her neck some indescribable little dead animal bit its own tail, its fur standing up wet and sticky like the fur of a drowned kitten. D. She was dressed in a brown jacket and a narrow brown skirt and in her bare hands she clutched a broken down-looking leather bag—the outside pockets bulging with what looked like old torn-up envelopes. S2: She stood as though she were part of the furniture of the station and had been there for years—an old automatic machine that nobody dreamed of slipping a coin into.
questions.questionHtml:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact.

S1: There was a woman on the station platform. A tall scrag of a woman wearing a little round hat with a brown feather that dropped in a draggled fringe over her eyes.

A. The toss and tumble, the hurrying threading rush of movement left her high and dry.
B. Brown button boots showed under the skirt and an end of white petticoat dabbled with mud.
C. Round her neck some indescribable little dead animal bit its own tail, its fur standing up wet and sticky like the fur of a drowned kitten.
D. She was dressed in a brown jacket and a narrow brown skirt and in her bare hands she clutched a broken down-looking leather bag—the outside pockets bulging with what looked like old torn-up envelopes.

S2: She stood as though she were part of the furniture of the station and had been there for years—an old automatic machine that nobody dreamed of slipping a coin into.
questions.solution:
Explanation:

S1

There was a woman on the station platform. A tall scrag of a woman wearing a little round hat with a brown feather that dropped in a draggled fringe over her eyes.

After introducing the woman, the paragraph should continue describing her appearance and belongings logically.

Sentence analysis

D
She was dressed in a brown jacket and a narrow brown skirt and in her bare hands she clutched a broken down-looking leather bag…

This gives the overall description of her clothing and the bag, so it naturally follows S1.

C
Round her neck some indescribable little dead animal bit its own tail…

This adds another detail of her appearance (neck accessory).

B
Brown button boots showed under the skirt and an end of white petticoat dabbled with mud.

Now the description moves downwards to the lower part of her body (boots).

A
The toss and tumble, the hurrying threading rush of movement left her high and dry.

This sentence shifts from description of appearance to the environment, preparing for S2.

Final sequence

S1 → D → C → B → A → S2

questions.question: The internal and external diameters of a hollow hemispherical bowl are 12 cm and 24 cm respectively. If it is melted and cast into a solid cylinder of diameter 12 cm, what will be the height of the cylinder (in cm)?
questions.questionHtml: The internal and external diameters of a hollow hemispherical bowl are 12 cm and 24 cm respectively. If it is melted and cast into a solid cylinder of diameter 12 cm, what will be the height of the cylinder (in cm)?
questions.solution:
External radius = 12
Internal radius = 6

Volume of hollow hemisphere

= (2/3)π(12³ − 6³)
= (2/3)π(1728 − 216)
= 1008π

Cylinder radius = 6

Volume of cylinder

= πr²h
= 36πh

36πh = 1008π

h = 28 cm

questions.question: The base of a right prism is a triangle with sides 20 cm, 21 cm, and 29 cm. Its height is 25 cm. Find the lateral surface area (in cm²) and the volume (in cm³) respectively.
questions.questionHtml: The base of a right prism is a triangle with sides 20 cm, 21 cm, and 29 cm. Its height is 25 cm. Find the lateral surface area (in cm²) and the volume (in cm³) respectively.
questions.solution:
20² + 21² = 29² ⇒ Right triangle

Base area = (1/2) × 20 × 21 = 210

Perimeter = 20 + 21 + 29 = 70

LSA = perimeter × height
= 70 × 25 = 1750 cm²

Volume = base area × height
= 210 × 25 = 5250 cm³
